topic: the two Hittite spies who deliberately got captured to feed Ramesses II false intel before Kadesh
title: The Fake Spies Who Nearly Destroyed Ramesses the Great's Army
description: AI-narrated commentary. In 1274 BC, two Hittite agents let themselves get captured by Ramesses the Great's scouts and fed him false intel about where the enemy army actually was -- a deliberate deception that nearly cost Egypt the Battle of Kadesh.

hook_candidates.text: Ramesses the Great nearly lost his whole army because he believed two guys his own men had just captured.
Two men let themselves get captured on purpose, just so they could lie straight to a pharaoh's face.
Why would two enemy spies want to get captured by the exact army they were spying on?
Getting captured wasn't these spies' mistake -- it was the entire plan.

payoff_mechanism: The Hittite king deliberately sent two men to be captured by Egyptian scouts, knowing Ramesses would interrogate them and trust what they said under questioning, so when they claimed the Hittite army was still far away near Aleppo, Ramesses split his forces and advanced with only one division, walking straight into thousands of hidden chariots waiting just behind the city.
share_trigger: A viewer sends this to the friend who just took someone's word for something big without double-checking it first, because they want to show even a legendary pharaoh got played by a well-timed lie.
contradicted_belief: Most people assume getting captured by the enemy is a spy's worst-case failure, but for these two men, getting captured on purpose was the entire winning strategy.

sources.note: Describes the two Hittite spies who let themselves be captured and fed Ramesses II false army-location intel before Kadesh.

beats.text: Two men let themselves get **captured** on purpose, just so they could lie straight to a pharaoh's face.
It was **1274 BC**, and Ramesses the Great was marching on the city of Kadesh.
His scouts caught two men claiming to be deserters. They swore the enemy army was still **far** away, near Aleppo.
Ramesses believed them, and pushed forward with just one division, **splitting** his own army wide open.

The real Hittite army was hiding right behind the city, **thousands** of chariots deep, waiting for exactly that mistake. Those two 'captured' men were never caught -- they were **sent**. There's a new one of these every few hours -- follow if you want the next.
